tip: 'Tenir' usually means 'to hold,' but 'il ne tient qu'à vous' means 'it rests entirely on you.' The 'ne...qu'à' narrows it to 'only you' – it's up to you alone.
'À bon chat, bon rat' is literally 'to a good cat, a good rat' – a sharp attacker meets an equally sharp defender. Evenly matched.
'Aucun' normally means 'none', but 'd'aucuns' flips it: an old plural for 'some people'. 'D'aucuns diront' = some will say.
'Errare humanum est' is Latin – 'to err is human' – dropped whole into formal French. It often continues: 'perseverare diabolicum' (to persist, diabolical).
'Vaille' is the subjunctive of 'valoir' (to be worth), frozen twice: 'vaille que vaille' literally 'be it worth what it may' = come what may.
'Est-il' here isn't a question – French inverts the verb after certain set openers. 'Toujours est-il que' = the fact remains that.
'C'est à' + infinitive: 'c'est à se demander' = it makes you wonder. A set pattern: the situation is enough to make you react that way.
